messages:
Maya L: Heads up na-west (na3) serving region seeing a large 95th/99th latency spike on realtime routes since 08:12 UTC. spikes correlate with hotpool saturation and continuous-batcher stalls. logs show KV cache slowpath and scheduler backpressure.
Ajay R: Noted. Is this across all GPU pools or specific to hotpools?
Maya L: Mostly hotpool-*-g4 and hotpool-*-a100. Standard reserved pools seem OK. Heap and GPU utilization at 95% on hotpools.
Sarah (runtime): throwing a quick grep: `grep -E \"kv_cache.*slowpath|batcher.*stall\" /var/log/runtime/*.log | tail -n 200` shows repeated `KVCache::deserialize_lock` timeouts and `continuous_batcher: flush_due_to_deadline` churn.
Igor: I'm seeing scheduler RPC queue depth rising (sched_proxy qdepth ~1200). The scheduling throttle kicked in and started rejecting placements which pushed more traffic to hotpools -> feedback loop.
Leo - infra: Traffic has been partially shifted to na-east by the smart-router but affinity rules kept a lot of sticky sessions to na-west. We can relax affinity for a subset of routes.
Maya L: We need emergency mitigations: 1) reduce continuous batching aggressiveness 2) desaturate hotpools (drain some tasks to reserved pools) 3) widen routing to na-east/na2 for non-SLA routes.
Sarah (runtime): I can flip the batcher gating to `max_batch_ms=10` and `min_batch_size=1` for affected services to cut queuing. Patching now.
Ajay R: Also suggest incrementally raising `kv_cache.deser_threads` from 8 -> 24 on hotpool nodes; riskier but should reduce slowpath. Would prefer safe incremental roll.
Igor: Rolling `deser_threads` needs node restart? We can do live config if runtime supports it. If not, do rolling restart with 10% concurrency.
Leo - infra: Starting a 10% hotpool desaturation now: `./control desaturate --pool hotpool-na3 --pct 10 --target reserved-pool-na3` (dry-run then apply).
OpsBot: incident created INC-2026-0318-01: "na3 hotpool desaturation + kv slowpath -> latency spike" assigned to eng-infra, eng-runtime.
Maya L: Good. Also temporarily disable prefixcache prefetch for the worst offending model routes (embedding-rerank / chat-short) to reduce KV pressure.
Sarah (runtime): Patch applied: batcher params updated for service: chat-realtime, generation-lowlatency. Observed immediate drop in batcher queue depth.
Ajay R: `deser_threads` ramp plan: +8 -> +8 -> +8 across 3 waves with 2m observation windows, starting now on 3 nodes.
Igor: Scheduler backpressure easing after first wave; qdepth down to ~400. Hotpool GPU util down 8%.
Leo - infra: Traffic shift executed for non-SLA routes: ~18% of requests to na-east. Logs show increased p95 for those routes by ~10ms (expected).
Maya L: Monitoring token-level latency and error rates. If p99 doesn't drop within 15m we escalate to capacity increase (spin ephemeral nodes).
Runbook Bot: Recommended runbook: "hotpool desaturation > reduce batching > increase KV deser threads > widen routing". Next step: consider model fallback to quantized variant for heavy routes.
Sarah (runtime): Running quick eval on fallback model quality for chat-long; looks acceptable for emergency. I'll gate rollout behind an approval from Maya/Ajay.
Maya L: Approve hot fallback for chat-long, 5% traffic can be diverted if needed.
Ajay R: Monitoring window shows p99 down ~35% and error rate stable. Keeping slowpath patches in canary for 30m then roll further.
Igor: Creating follow-up ticket to investigate root cause: potential memory churn in KV cache serializer after recent kernel bump; collect core dumps and perf traces.
Maya L: Thanks team. Keep status updates here. If anyone sees a regression from the patch, flag immediately. :thumbsup:
